 Advocate for : MR. J LASKAR  Advocate for : SC  REVENUE appearing for THE STATE OF ASSAM AND 7 ORS  BEFORE  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE MANISH CHOUDHURY  ORDER 16.05.2024 Heard Mr. B. Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioner in W.P.[C] no. 7220/2015;

Mr.
A.K. Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioners in W.P.[C] no. 1586/2015; Mr. R. Borpujari,
learned Standing Counsel, Revenue Department; Mr. R.K. Talukdar, learned Standing Counsel,
NHIDCL; and Mr. B.J. Talukdar, learned senior counsel assisted by Mr. P.K. Medhi, learned penal advocate for other State respondents.

2. The relevant excerpts of the Order passed on 28.06.2022 were as under :-
Page No.# 4/6 The state respondents in both the writ petitions are to clarify on the following aspects : [i] publication of the notification under Section 4[1], Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in the Gazette and through the newspapers; [ii] publication of the Declarations under Section 6[1], Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in the Gazette and through the newspapers; [iii] finalization of the award by the Collector; [iv] approval by the Government to the award; and [v] disbursal of the compensation amounts, if any; by way of additional affidavits.

sentences.text: In deference to the order dated 28.06.2022, additional affidavits are filed in both the cases.

After perusal of the materials brought through such additional affidavits in respect of the land acquisition cases, that is, L.A. Case no. 32/2009, L.A. Case no. 33/2009, L.A. Case no. 35/2009, L.A. Case no.
36/2009, L.A. Case no. 37/2009 and L.A. Case no. 44/2009, this Court in its order dared 14.11.2022 had observed as under :-
In LA Case No.32/2009 it has been mentioned that the notification in the Official Gazette under Section 4 (1) of the Act of 1894 issued on 19.11.2013.
A perusal of the said notification reveals that there was a dispensation of Section 5 A of the Act of 1894 by invoking the urgency clause stipulated in Section 17 (4) of the Act of 1894.

It further reveals that the declaration under Section 6 of the Act of 1894 was issued on 28.11.2013 which was published in the Assam Gazette on 05.12.2013 and the same was subsequently published in a local Daily Newspaper on 31.01.2014.

It is however surprises this Court to take note of that the Competent Authority though had proceeded under Section 6 of the Act of 1894 but complied with one of the mandatory modes of publication under Section 4 (1) of the Act of 1894 only on 31.01.2014.

It further surprises this Court that the award was forwarded by the Collector on 30.12.2013 to the Government for approval and the Government approved it in terms with the proviso to Section 11 (1) of the Act of 1894 only on 06.01.2014 but Section 4 (1) of the Act of 1894 was complied only on 30.01.2014.
It further is apparent that as the approval for the State Government came only on 06.01.2014, the award can only be published in terms with Section 12 (2) of the Act of 1894 on or after 06.01.2014.

Similarly, upon perusal of the additional affidavit filed and the details given in LA Case No.33/2009;
LA Case No.35/2009; LA Case No.36/2009; LA Case No.37/2009 and LA Case No.44/2009, the compliance after the approval being received from the appropriate Government authorities only after 01.01.2014 and consequently the passing of the award would be after 01.01.2014.

It is also relevant to take note of that if any other interpretation is being given, the said award would be in the teeth of Section 4 and Section 6 of the Act of 1894 taking into consideration that Page No.# 5/6 the last of the said notification as required under Section 4 (1) of the Act of 1894 happened only on 31.01.2014 which is the notification to be taken into consideration as the date of the notification.
Therefore, all the awards passed in the above noted LA Cases has to be deemed to have passed after 01.01.2014.

In view of the notification dated 19.12.2013, published by the Ministry of Road and Surface Transport, Government of India, the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, the Act of 2013) comes into effect with effect from 01.01.2014.

(a) of the Act of 2013 which stipulates that if Land Acquisition proceedings have been initiated under the Act of 1894 and the award was passed subsequent to coming into effect the Act of 2013,
the determination of compensation has to be made in terms with the Act of 2013.

sentences.text: Now coming to the fact of the case in WP(C) No.7220/2015 which relates to LA Case No.47/2009, it appears from the said additional affidavit filed by the respondent No.3 on 01.08.2022 that the notification under Section 4 of the Act of 1894 was published on 19.10.2013 in Official Gazette and the said notification under Section 4 of the Act of 1894 was published in the local Daily Newspaper on 19.01.2014.
As in the case of Section 6 of the Act of 1894, the notification in the Official Gazette was issued on 23.12.2013 and the same was published in the local Daily Newspaper on 31.01.2014.

Further it appears that although the award was forwarded by the Government on 27.12.2013, but it was approved by the Government on 29.01.2014 and the said amount was sanctioned by the respondent No.3 only on 15.02.2014.

Therefore, it would also appear that taking into note of Section 12 (2) of the Act of 1894, the award was filed only after coming into effect the Act of 2013, and therefore, the compensation has to be determined in terms with the Act of 2013 for the reason already mentioned herein above.
Taking into consideration the above and also the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioners to the effect that they are interested only on the question of the quantum of compensation as to whether it should be determined as per the Act of 1894 or the Act of 2013 and the submission made by Mr. R. Borpujari, the learned counsel, Revenue Department to the effect that the Government wants to retain the land on the ground that the Government has already spent a huge amount of money on creating of the infrastructure on the said acquired land, this Court is of the opinion that it would be in the interest of justice to grant some time to the State respondents to take a position as to whether they would like to retain the land by paying compensation in terms with the Act of 2013 or give up the claims in respect to the land.
Accordingly, let the matter be taken up on 19.01.2023 for further consideration.
Page No.# 6/6
In the meantime, the respondent authorities shall apprise this Court as regards their intention by filing an affidavit.

4. Mr. Barpujari, learned Standing Counsel, Revenue Department has sought for 3 [three] weeks'
time to file an additional affidavit in deference to the order dated 14.11.2022.
5.
The prayer made by Mr. Borpujari is allowed.

6. List the cases on 18.06.2024.
7.
For the purpose of facilitating Mr. Borpujari to obtain instructions and to file the additional affidavit, a copy of this order be supplied to Mr. Borpujari.
